messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: GPU-host-health-us-west1 - multiple host reboots detected, error rate spike on /v1/generate, customers affected. Pager severity: P1.

devon (oncall): ack. I'm on it. seeing ~18% 5xx for inference-prod-us-west over last 10m. moving to #oncall-handoff.

maria (sre): pinging infra and ml infra. do we have a quick blast radius? which clusters/nodes?

chris (infra): initial check: it's concentrated in us-west1-a across hosts in the gpu-pool-2 autoscale group. 7 hosts reported unexpected reboots in the last 40m. cloud provider shows hypervisor events on those hosts.

nina (ml infra): product impact: a few mid-tier customers reported repeated streaming disconnects; embedding jobs auto-restarted. I'll gather traces.

eli (engineer): attaching recent node logs I pulled from one affected host (host-azw-08):

```
Mar 26 02:11:07 host kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:0b:00): 79, pid=2456, 16c8
Mar 26 02:11:07 host kernel: pciehp 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: severity=Corrected, tlp=0001, desc=Data Link Protocol
Mar 26 02:11:08 host kernel: kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000020
Mar 26 02:11:08 host kernel: Code: Bad RIP value.
```

chris (infra): thanks eli. also seeing repeated ECC single-bit corrections from nvidia-smi before the panics: `ECC errors: single-bit 127 -> corrected` and then a spike to multi-bit on one host.

maria (sre): timeline so far (rough): 01:42 first alert from autoscaler, 01:50 first host reboot, 02:10 spike in corrected ECC counts on hosts 05-09, 02:11 host kernel oops + reboot, 02:30 rollout of cordon+drain for suspected hosts, 02:45 fallback routing enabled to us-east1.

devon (oncall): mitigation in place: cordoned 5 hosts, draining running jobs, forced traffic to dedicated-fallback pool. Respawn workers on healthy nodes. Still seeing intermittent 502s for long-tail streaming sessions.

nina (ml infra): capture: attaching example span showing kill/restart of worker while streaming. customer request id 7c2f-9b: they saw partial stream then `connection reset by peer`.

eli (engineer): hypothesis 1: noisy neighbor causing PCIe link errors -> driver inconsistencies -> kernel OOPS. hypothesis 2: firmware regression in host BMC/NIC causing ECC reporting corruption which escalates to driver panic under load.

chris (infra): supporting data: provider's hypervisor logs show DIMM ECC events correlated with same host reboot times. provider ticket opened (see cloud-support-bot for link).

cloud-support-bot: Ticket #CS-84219 created with cloud provider. Initial summary: "Host-level memory ECC corrections followed by kernel oops on guest. Provider investigating possible firmware/firmware-update rollouts in region."

maria (sre): OK. we need a focused investigation plan: 1) capture full dmesg+journal from earliest affected hosts, 2) preserve crash kernel if kdump available, 3) confirm if any kernel/driver updates rolled recently by provider, 4) isolate hosts to prevent further customer impact.

devon (oncall): doing 1 & 2 now on hosts host-azw-05..host-azw-09. chris, can infra freeze the autoscaler for gpu-pool-2? want to avoid noisy placement flips.

chris (infra): autoscale frozen for gpu-pool-2. also blocking new launches on same placement group.

eli (engineer): past 24h package diffs on our side show no GPU driver changes. only recent platform change was wider rollout of kernel 5.14.23 two nights ago in us-west1. but affected hosts include some still on 5.14.22, so mixed.

nina (ml infra): running a controlled repro: spinning up stress-ng memory workload pinned to GPU containers on a test host with same HW profile. will report if we can reproduce ECC correction ramp.\n

maria (sre): good. I'll start building timeline artifact in our RCA doc and paste logs here as we go. please prefix any pasted logs with host id.

eli (engineer): paste from host-azw-08 nvidia-smi -q excerpt:

```
GPU 0:
  FB Memory ECC Errors
    Volatile
      Single-bit ECC: 142
      Double-bit ECC: 1
```

eli (engineer): host dmesg snippet (host-azw-08):

```
[12345.678901] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x24:0x46:145)
[12345.679012] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[12345.679123] kernel: ata1: exception Emask 0x0 SAct 0x0 SErr 0x40
```

chris (infra): pulled provider placement metadata: these hosts are on machines with firmware version 3.7.8. Provider said they had no automatic firmware pushes in the last 48h but will re-check.

cloud-support-bot: Update: Provider initial triage: they see a pattern of corrected ECC counts followed by a subset of guests hitting kernel oops; suspect hardware DIMM issues on physical hosts. Provider has scheduled health checks + planned host evacuation for flagged machines.

maria (sre): annotating timeline: please add exact timestamps for each log blob. we'll use this to correlate with provider events.

devon (oncall): customers impacted list so far: cust-ink (embedding API), cust-halo (chat low-latency tier). notifed SRE/customer-success leads and opened incident pages for affected accounts.

eli (engineer): quick experiment: applied `nvidia-smi --reset-ecc` on a test host (no traffic) and monitored. Single-bit counts stopped accumulating but after ~30m reappeared. suggests underlying physical/memory issue rather than driver leak.

nina (ml infra): repro test result: stress workload triggered ECC correction spike on test host within 18m, and kernel panics after sustained corrections on that machine. capturing execs now.

maria (sre): immediate mitigation actions checklist (in-flight): cordon+drain affected hosts (done), freeze autoscaler (done), redirect traffic to fallback pool (done), notify customers (devon done), escalate to provider (cloud-support-bot). Next: schedule bulk repro windows and decide about emergency host replacement if provider confirms DIMM faults.

chris (infra): recommended short-term: mark hosts as quarantined and shift reserved capacity from dedicated-fallback to cover steady traffic. triggering reserved capacity now.

devon (oncall): will keep the page open until provider confirms host remediation or we've replaced hosts.

cloud-support-bot: Provider update 03:40 UTC: manual inspection found 2 hosts with degraded DIMM channels; provider scheduling hardware replacement and pausing further maintenance in that rack.

eli (engineer): adding hypothesis 3: there's an interaction between kernel 5.14.23 + existing firmware that surfaces ECC multi-bit on stressed GPU memory paths. Need matrix test across kernel/firmware combos.

nina (ml infra): agree. I'll orchestrate canary runs: kernel 5.14.22 vs 5.14.23 on identical HW, stress GPU/memory. schedule in next 6h.

maria (sre): I'll collect kdump files if we get another panic and stash them in the RCA doc. Also capturing full stack traces of crashed kernels.

devon (oncall): status: tailing logs. currently error rate down to ~3% since fallback routing. will update if we get more host crashes.

chris (infra): infra action item: prepare list of hosts to replace and coordinate with provider support for replacement windows. assigning to chris.

eli (engineer): engineering action item: create repro matrix and run overnight. assigning to eli & nina.

maria (sre): post-incident action items: 1) improve early ECC spike alerts, 2) add cross-check between hypervisor ECC reports and guest nvidia-smi to catch issues earlier, 3) playbook update for GPU host corruptions.

devon (oncall): thanks all. I'll hand this to morning oncall but will stay if provider updates. keeping thread pinned. :white_check_mark:

cloud-support-bot: Provider final update (04:50 UTC): replacements completed for flagged hosts; no broader firmware rollout detected. Provider recommends monitoring for 24h and will keep ticket open.

maria (sre): logging final interim conclusion: immediate customer impact mitigated by quarantine + fallback routing. Working hypothesis: host DIMM/channel degradation causing ECC corrections escalating to kernel oops on guests; further testing needed on kernel/firmware interaction. RCA doc link: https://rdrive.redwood/intranet/rca/1947654321. Action items assigned. Closing active paging stage; follow-up postmortem planned.

devon (oncall): handing over to next-day oncall. leaving summary in ops-notes. If anything spikes, re-open page.

incidents-bot: Incident status changed to MONITOR. Page unassigned."
